newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia minerals industry more profitable.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia minerals industry more profitable.

text.p: Australia's minerals industry was more profitable in 1995/96 (July-June) than in the previous year, the Minerals Council of Australia said on Wednesday.
A survey undertaken for the council by Coopers and Lybrand said net profit return on average shareholders funds was 8.8 percent in 1996/96, compared with 5.3 percent a year earlier.
But the latest figure was still below the 10-year average of 11.8 percent, the survey said.
Overall mine production was higher in 1995/96, with gold up 10 percent, iron ore up 4.0 percent and coal rising 2.0 percent, survey figures show.
Mine output of copper ws up 18 percent, lead rose 3.0 percent and zinc climbed 7.0 percent.
Projects with a total value of about A$6 billion were under construction as of June 1996, including A$2.6 billion in the coal sector alone, it noted.

In launching the survey, the council's president and the incoming chairman of the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, Jerry Ellis, said there was a trend toward "internationalisation" of Australian minerals companies.
During 1995/96, spending on gold and platinum exploration accounted for 45 percent of the total overseas spending by respondents," Ellis said in a statement.
A further 26 percent was spent in base metals exploration and 14 percent in diamond hunts, he said.
